To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best Time Series model for predicting enrollment for undergraduate CS courses at CSUN is the R model using the ARIMA(2,0,0) method with a maximum of 6 semesters of data used for training.
the best predictions for course enrollment in the CSD are obtained by using the Weka models with 3 semesters of hold out data.

the best predictions were made by a Time Series model using Weka, which predicted 93.5 percent of Computer Science courses accurately within one class size of 30 students, and the worst prediction was made by a Time series model using Weka that predicted 77.4 percent of Computer Science classes accurately within one class of 30 students.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

all of the models tested in this paper can predict enrollment in CS and CIT undergraduate courses to within one class size of 20-25 students with a high degree of accuracy, and that all of the tested models perform better when using a maximum amount of available enrollment data.
the best model for the CSD was the Holt Winters model, and the best model for CIT was the Weka Time Series model.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the Weka models were generally more accurate than the R models, and that predictions for CSD and CIT courses were more accurate when using unmodified values than when modified to round up and zero out negative predictions.
Weka’s ARIMA and ARMA models were the most accurate for both departments, but Weka’s ARMA model was most accurate for the CSD.

the R models are better at predicting the enrollment of Computer Science and Computer Information Technology courses than the Weka models, and the R models are most accurate when predicting the next three semesters of enrollment using all of the enrollment data from the previous 5 semesters.
